alternative_explanations: Surface parsing and the disclosed iterative traversal scaffold may explain learned-control success without general language understanding.
The synthetic grammar may make the symbolic control dominant and overstate real-world update reliability.
confounds: One runner-random seed cannot estimate seed variability.
The calibration reader is not the future one-shot 8192-token dense reference.
falsification_criteria: Any missing KxD cell, leakage, parser failure above threshold, timeout, OOM, crash, or omitted full-boundary cost makes the calibration inconclusive and ends the stage without retry.
Dense overall accuracy below 0.85 or replacement accuracy below 0.80 rejects the learned-control calibration even if the symbolic control is exact.

invalidation_rules: Invalidate if any final answer, private map, path, query stratum or generator state reaches a system before its prediction.
Invalidate if train, development and calibration worlds or entity namespaces overlap.
Invalidate if any system receives different serialized statements or questions for the same cell.
Invalidate if the symbolic parser receives generator objects rather than the same raw UTF-8 text.
Invalidate if any learned role uses pretrained weights, an external model, an API, network access or test-guided tuning.
Invalidate if fit, text processing, index construction, update, query, state, RSS or VRAM cost is omitted.
Invalidate on a missing KxD cell, context truncation, nonfinite result, timeout, OOM, crash or evaluator-integrity change.
Stop after exactly one registered runner-random calibration attempt; no retry or replacement registration.

outcome_policy.negative: If evaluator integrity or the symbolic control fails, treat the task calibration as invalid or inconclusive, preserve all artifacts, and stop.
outcome_policy.null: If symbolic is valid but learned controls are not competent, reject this calibration recipe and stop without test-guided repair.
outcome_policy.positive: Record that task and controls are operationally valid, identify the strongest baseline and one next discriminating local-memory experiment, then stop for user review.

predicted_outcome: The symbolic control should be exact, while both learned controls should exceed the frozen competence thresholds and expose the expected dense versus retrieval cost difference.
promotion_criteria: No architecture may be promoted; a valid calibration only supports asking for one separately authorized local-memory mechanism experiment.
research_question: Do the frozen mutable-ledger task, learned transformer and retrieval controls, and symbolic last-write control provide a valid fully accounted calibration across fact scale, replacement, and composition depth?
title: MUC-01 single baseline calibration
